title: 2006 AMC 12B Problem 10
statement: In a triangle with integer side lengths, one side is three times as long as a second side, and the length of the third side is \(15.\) What is the greatest possible perimeter of the triangle?

solutions.text:
Let the sides be \(x,\) \(3x,\) and \(15.\) The triangle inequality requires \(x + 3x \gt 15,\) so \(x \geq 4,\) and \(x + 15 \gt 3x,\) so \(x \leq 7.\)

The perimeter \(4x + 15\) is largest when \(x = 7,\) giving \(7 + 21 + 15 = 43.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let the sides be \(x,\) \(3x,\) and \(15,\) then apply the triangle inequality
The binding condition is \(x + 15 \gt 3x,\) which caps how large \(x\) can be
